headlines.title: 무디스 “ 韓 메모리 대체할 곳 없다 ”… 성장률 전망 1.8%→3.5 %
headlines.summary: 2월 1.8%→5월 2.5%→8월 3.5% “고급 메모리 대체공급업체 제한적” ‘3대 메가프로젝트’도 긍정적 평가 국제신용평가사 무디스가 올해 한국 경제성장률 전망치를 3.5%로 대폭 끌어올렸다. 인공지능(AI) 투자 확대에 따른 반도체 ‘슈퍼사이클’이 적어도 내년 중반까지 이어지고 수출 호조도 지속될 것이란 판단이 반영됐다.

headlines.title: “ 전세 살 바엔 집 사자 ”… 서울 집값 기대심리 1년 새 최고

key_headlines.title: Seoul Housing Prices Hit One-Year High Expectations Amid Shift from Jeonse to Purchase
key_headlines.summary: Consumer sentiment toward Seoul housing prices reached the highest level in one year in July, with expectations for price increases and transaction growth rising. The shift from jeonse (long-term lease) to home purchases reflects changing demand patterns in the real estate market.

key_headlines.title: Moody's Upgrades Korea's 2026 Growth Rate to 3.5% on Semiconductor Supercycle
key_headlines.summary: International credit rating agency Moody's significantly raised South Korea's economic growth forecast to 3.5% for 2026, citing the semiconductor supercycle driven by AI investment expansion and sustained export momentum. The agency emphasized that advanced memory semiconductors have limited alternative suppliers globally.

key_headlines.title: Government Launches Youth Housing Loan Program with 80% LTV for Non-Apartment Properties
key_headlines.summary: The government will introduce a Youth Future Housing Loan starting January 2027, offering up to 80% loan-to-value ratio for first-time homebuyers purchasing non-apartment properties under 400 million won. This policy aims to support housing accessibility for young people while stimulating redevelopment investment.

key_headlines.title: Low-Income Single-Person Households Most Vulnerable to Inflation Impact
key_headlines.summary: Analysis shows that low-income single-person households face greater burden from price increases than the overall consumer inflation rate, as they concentrate spending on essential goods like food and housing. Policy recommendations suggest fiscal measures should reflect these vulnerabilities.

key_headlines.title: 54-Year-Old Education Subsidy Formula to be Reformed with Economic Growth-Based Model
key_headlines.summary: The government is discontinuing the internal tax revenue linking system for education subsidies, replacing it with a formula incorporating economic growth rates, school-age population, and inflation. This reform allows for budget adjustments based on actual education demand with a floor at 95% of the previous year's budget.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's housing market continues to show strong momentum with Seoul apartment prices rising 1.09% month-over-month in July, marking the fourth consecutive month of accelerating gains. Consumer sentiment toward housing prices has reached its highest level in one year, with more households shifting preferences from jeonse leases to home purchases as actual purchasing sentiment strengthens. The government has introduced new housing support policies, including a Youth Future Housing Loan program starting January 2027 that offers up to 80% LTV ratios for qualifying first-time buyers. Meanwhile, Moody's substantially upgraded Korea's 2026 economic growth forecast to 3.5%, citing the strength of the semiconductor supercycle and robust export performance.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Moody's raised South Korea's 2026 GDP growth forecast to 3.5%, up from 2.5% in May and 1.8% in February, reflecting confidence in sustained semiconductor demand and export growth. The government is reforming the 54-year-old education subsidy formula by eliminating the internal tax revenue linking system and replacing it with a model incorporating economic growth rates, school-age population, and inflation factors. Korea's fiscal deficit ratio is expected at 3.8% of GDP, slightly below the previous 3.9% target, though long-term fiscal sustainability concerns remain due to aging demographics. Taiwan announced record GDP growth of 11.05% for 2026 and plans to distribute cash bonuses worth approximately 440,000 won per citizen from surplus tax revenues.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI index declined 1.5% after five consecutive days of gains, pressured by rising global bond yields and geopolitical tensions. U.S. 30-year Treasury yields reached 5.31%, the highest level since 2007, reflecting concerns about national debt and inflation expectations. The Equity Risk Premium has been declining as higher bond yields reduce the relative attractiveness of stocks compared to bonds in a high-interest environment. Semiconductor stocks continue to attract investor focus, with major chipmakers like Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix leading gains on the KOSPI, while smaller semiconductor suppliers gain on the KOSDAQ.
sections.Industry & Technology: The government is preparing the 12th Basic Electricity Plan and has not yet decided on the role of nuclear power, citing the need to reassess electricity demand forecasts given recent semiconductor and data center requirements. Multiple startups across semiconductors, biotech, and other advanced technology sectors are securing investments to address the growing demand for specialized chip solutions and healthcare devices. Alibaba Cloud opened its third domestic data center in South Korea to address growing AI infrastructure demand. Electric vehicles face challenges during heavy flooding as battery systems typically installed across the vehicle floor are vulnerable to water submersion.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment prices continued their strong upward trajectory in July with an increase of 1.09% month-over-month, marking the fourth consecutive month of accelerating gains. The transition from jeonse (long-term lease) to monthly rental properties accelerated, with monthly rentals increasing by 52,000 units while jeonse decreased by 35,000 units, shifting the rental composition from 30.3% to 38.1% over the past seven years. Despite strong government regulation measures, housing prices and rental rates have both increased significantly, making home ownership increasingly challenging for ordinary citizens. The government's new Youth Future Housing Loan program aims to ease entry barriers for first-time homebuyers while raising concerns about stimulating redevelopment speculation.
sections.International Economy: Global bond yields have risen significantly, with U.S. 10-year Treasury yields exceeding 4.7% and 30-year yields reaching their highest level in 19 years, driven by national debt concerns and inflation expectations. The yen weakened to the 159 range against the dollar despite potential Japanese central bank interventions, reflecting broader currency market pressures. Japan's second quarter GDP growth of 0.3% came in below expectations, though nominal growth reached record highs, prompting discussion of earlier Bank of Japan rate increases. Korea's Industry Minister visited Washington to discuss U.S. investment projects and address tariff concerns amid trade negotiations, as the government faces pressure to accelerate semiconductor manufacturing investments in the United States.
sections.AI & Economy: Alibaba Cloud launched its third domestic data center in Seoul within one year to meet surging Korean AI infrastructure demand as part of its 53 billion dollar global initiative. AI-driven datacenter investment expansion has caused global NAND flash memory sales for the top five companies to surge 77%, with Micron rising to third place globally. The government, through the Industrial Bank, is supporting investment in promising startups focused on defense and physical AI technologies. AI datacenters are becoming critical infrastructure, with KMAC undertaking a master plan for Korean Electric Power's AI datacenter construction to support energy sector digital transformation.
sections.Others: The government reformed the lottery revenue distribution system after 22 years, eliminating mandatory allocations to eight agencies while maintaining allocations to local governments and Jeju Province, shifting to performance-based funding. Industry Minister Kim Jung-gwan made an emergency visit to Washington to address U.S. investment commitments and clarify policy direction following the sudden resignation of the chief trade negotiator. SK Hynix appointed a new vice president of international finance with IMF experience to strengthen capabilities for managing U.S. investment projects and semiconductor factory expansion. An AI analysis of major Japanese companies' potential market performance by year-end revealed varied economic scenarios depending on which companies lead the market capitalization rankings.
